claims.text: HEAs processed under tailored conditions to achieve an optimal microstructure will exhibit superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared with traditional structural alloys.
The initial material is an as-cast HEA with a multi-principal-element composition.
Tailoring processing temperature, time, and atmosphere can produce an optimal HEA microstructure.
The relevant service environment combines elevated temperature with tribo-corrosion.
Grain size and distribution mediate the effect of processing on degradation resistance.
Phase composition mediates the effect of processing on degradation resistance.
Defect density mediates the effect of processing on degradation resistance.
A tailored HEA microstructure enhances formation of a protective oxide layer.
A tailored HEA microstructure reduces diffusion of corrosive species.
A tailored HEA microstructure improves mechanical properties.
Protective oxide formation, reduced corrosive-species diffusion, and improved mechanical properties lead to superior degradation resistance.
The tailored HEA will have a 30% lower degradation rate than traditional structural alloys under the same conditions.
Degradation rate will be measured as mass loss per unit area per unit time in g/m^2/h.
The optimal microstructure has a grain size of 10–50 μm.
The optimal microstructure has a uniform distribution of phases.
Actual degradation resistance may vary with HEA composition, processing conditions, and environmental factors.
